title: A Gravity for the Signal
premise: Ulyana Galloway, the last human technician aboard the automated relay station Perihelion, has kept her head down for twenty years hauling cargo through orbits claimed by three warring colonial factions. When children across the colony begin sharing an identical dream—a voice counting down from a dead relay at the edge of unmonitored space—she recognizes the signal's cadence as her late partner's, transmitted by a machine she helped decommission and never truly shut off. Pursued by the Colonial Authority, which wants the signal silenced before it destabilizes the ceasefire, Ulyana races toward the dead relay with a stowaway child who dreams loudest of all. She reaches the relay to find her partner's consciousness preserved in its buffers, and must choose between preserving his final message and broadcasting a warning that will end her invisibility forever. She broadcasts, loses him a second time, and returns to the colony no longer a ghost but a mother, a witness, and the signal's keeper.
about_author: Zephyrine Oyelaran is a former orbital logistics dispatcher who turned to fiction after two decades of logging cargo manifests in low Earth orbit. She writes near-future science fiction about the people machines forget, and lives between Lagos and a decommissioned weather station she refuses to name.

chapters.title: Manifest of Small Ghosts
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. A routine cargo haul through contested orbit establishes her careful, invisible life aboard the Perihelion—her rituals, her rationed memories, her refusal to answer hails from the colony below. Emotional beat: loneliness mistaken for peace, cracked open when she logs an anomalous ping from a relay officially listed as dead for fifteen years.

chapters.title: The Children Who Count Backward
chapters.summary: POV shifts to Idris, an eight-year-old in the colony's lower hab rings, who wakes reciting the same countdown as forty other children. His grandmother, a former signal analyst, recognizes the cadence and quietly contacts the station. Emotional beat: communal dread and wonder; Ulyana, receiving the message, feels twenty years of self-imposed exile begin to collapse.

chapters.title: Cadence of a Dead Man
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She decrypts the ping and finds the transmission signature of Tomas Reyes, her partner, lost during the decommissioning of Relay Kestrel at the edge of dead space. The Colonial Authority detects her queries and dispatches an auditor. Emotional beat: grief rekindled into purpose; she begins prepping the Perihelion for a run no cargo contract permits.

chapters.title: Stowaway in the Cold Hold
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. Fleeing the Authority's sweep of dreaming children, Idris smuggles himself aboard the Perihelion in a cryo crate. Ulyana discovers him mid-burn, past the point of turning back. Emotional beat: reluctant friction turning to tenderness as the boy's dream—Tomas's voice—guides her through a navigation corridor only the dead relay remembers.

chapters.title: Ceasefire Lines
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Running the gauntlet between three faction patrol zones, she bargains, bluffs, and burns fuel she cannot replace, while the Authority's auditor, Okafor, hails her with an offer: surrender the child, keep her station. Emotional beat: love against duty crystallizes—Ilyana realizes the duty she's been serving was never hers.

chapters.title: What the Buffers Keep
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. In dead space, the boy's dream sharpens into something like conversation; he describes Tomas's memories—Ulyana's laugh, a kitchen on Mars—that he could never know. Ulyana listens and breaks. Emotional beat: the found-family bond seals as she stops treating Idris as cargo and starts treating him as kin.

chapters.title: Relay Kestrel
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. They dock with the derelict relay and find Tomas's consciousness fragment intact in the buffers—neither alive nor dead, looping his last twenty years of transmissions toward her, unheard until now. Okafor's ship arrives in system. Emotional beat: reunion as wound; Ulyana must tell him he is an echo, and he asks her to finish what he started.

chapters.title: The Authority of Silence
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. Aboard the interceptor, Okafor—revealed to be a former colleague of both Ulyana and Tomas—grapples with orders to jam the signal, which carries a warning: the ceasefire's automated defense grid is failing, and the factions' own machines will fire on each other within days. Emotional beat: Okafor's duty fractures against conscience.

chapters.title: Counting Down to Zero
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, climax. With Okafor's ship jamming and Kestrel's power failing, Ulyana wires her own station's transmitter into the relay and lets Tomas's echo ride her signal home—broadcasting the warning and his final message to every dreaming child at once. The countdown reaches zero as the grid stands down. Emotional beat: sacrifice and release; the echo dissolves mid-word, and Ulyana lets it.

chapters.title: A Gravity for the Signal
chapters.summary: Idris's POV, resolution. Weeks later, the children's dreams have gone quiet, but Idris still hums the cadence. Ulyana, no longer invisible, takes a post teaching signal theory in the colony, with Okafor as reluctant ally. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into inheritance—the signal ends, but what it carried, love and warning, now has a home.
